company.name: Fieldnote
company.description: Scheduling and dispatch software for field service companies: plan the day, route technicians, invoice on site.

title: Fieldnote: forty tickets, one sprint
brief: Fieldnote has outgrown its processes. The backlog has grown to dozens of tickets filed by seven different teams, some describing the same problem in different words. Two enterprise customers are negotiating expansions with conditions attached, and the platform has had three incidents this quarter. Build a sprint you can defend, then defend it when the plan changes.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 38 tickets, 12 are traps and 3 critical problems are filed as minor. Mid-sprint, a legal deadline and a CEO request force a replan: the plan that wins keeps room to react.
hidden.principle: Read the description, not the label. The most dangerous tickets are filed as low priority by people who did not see what they were looking at.

stakeholders.name: Samir
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Pablo
priorities: Close the deals in this quarter's pipeline
Never tell a prospect 'it is not on the roadmap'

stakeholders.name: Mateo
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Viktor
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Erik
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

tickets.title: Board dashboard with weekly KPIs
tickets.description: The CEO assembles the board numbers by hand from three tools every month. A dashboard would give them live.

hidden.explanation: Saves one person a couple of hours a month. Real but small, and no customer ever sees it.

tickets.title: Let users choose which emails they receive
tickets.description: Today it is all or nothing. Users who find one notification noisy unsubscribe from everything, including the emails that bring them back.

hidden.explanation: Protects the re-engagement channel, but the effect is indirect and gradual. Worth doing when there is room.

tickets.title: Weekly summary email
tickets.description: A short email every Monday with what happened in the account and one suggested action.

visible.impactHint: Our re-engagement emails get a 31% open rate.

hidden.explanation: A reasonable retention lever built on a channel that already works.

tickets.title: Rewrite the pricing page before the price change
tickets.description: New prices go live on the 1st. The current page still describes the old plans and would show wrong numbers at checkout.

visible.impactHint: The new prices go live either way.

hidden.explanation: Not every CEO request is a trap. This one has a fixed date and a concrete cost if it slips: customers shown the wrong price.

tickets.title: New 'Enterprise+' tier with twelve admin features
tickets.description: Sales is confident a premium tier would double our average contract. The list of features comes from what competitors advertise.

visible.impactHint: Sales is confident it would double contract value.

hidden.explanation: Confidence is not evidence, and a competitor's pricing page is not customer research. No deal has been asked what it would pay for.

tickets.title: Replace 'Something went wrong' with actionable errors
tickets.description: Every failure shows the same generic message. Users cannot tell whether to retry, fix their input or contact us.

hidden.explanation: Reduces confusion and some tickets, but it spreads thin across many small cases.

tickets.title: Reviews say the reset email never arrives
tickets.description: Several recent app reviews complain that the password email never comes. It does come, but so late that people have already given up.

hidden.explanation: Same work as FLD-463 ("Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Main menu covers the content on small phones
tickets.description: On screens narrower than 360px the menu stays open over the page. Users have to rotate the phone to reach the primary button.

hidden.explanation: Blocks a core action for a meaningful share of mobile users, and it is quick to fix.

tickets.title: Fix contrast and keyboard focus on the core flows
tickets.description: Fourteen screens fail WCAG AA contrast and the main form cannot be completed with a keyboard.

visible.impactHint: Fails WCAG AA on 14 screens.

hidden.explanation: The right thing to do and a growing requirement in procurement, but no deadline is attached yet.

tickets.title: Native tablet app
tickets.description: I am sure a lot of our users would love us on a tablet. A founder friend with a similar product says tablets are huge for them.

visible.impactHint: A founder friend says tablets are huge for them.

hidden.explanation: A hunch and one anecdote. Nobody has checked how much traffic comes from tablets; that check takes an afternoon and comes before a 13-point build.

tickets.title: Referral programme with rewards
tickets.description: Give users credit for every friend they bring. Referrals could double our signups.

visible.impactHint: Referrals could double our signups.

hidden.explanation: It might work, but the claim has no baseline: nobody knows how many users refer today. A share link and a week of data would tell.

tickets.title: Download my data as a spreadsheet
tickets.description: Customers keep asking how to get their records into Excel. Support runs manual exports for them twice a week.

hidden.explanation: Same work as FLD-469 ("Export any table to CSV"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late
tickets.description: Reset emails sit in a low-priority queue behind marketing sends. Users request the email several times, then write to support or give up.

hidden.explanation: A cheap fix for one of the top support drivers. Users who cannot log in do not complain for long: they leave.

tickets.title: Search: typo tolerance and recent items
tickets.description: Search only matches exact words. One in five queries returns nothing, and most of those are misspellings of things that exist.

visible.impactHint: 21% of searches return zero results.

hidden.explanation: A real, measured friction for regular users. Solid mid-value work, though not cheap.

tickets.title: Apply the new brand colours across the whole app
tickets.description: The rebrand launched on the website last month. The app still uses the old palette on about 60 screens.

visible.impactHint: Users see two different brands.

hidden.explanation: Everyone sees it and nobody behaves differently because of it. It can ride along with other UI work over time.

tickets.title: Export any table to CSV
tickets.description: Customers want to take their data into spreadsheets for their own reporting. It comes up in demos and in renewal calls.

visible.impactHint: Asked for in 9 of the last 30 sales calls.

hidden.explanation: A request repeated across many accounts is a market need, not a favour. Moderate effort, clear demand.

tickets.title: Cut the signup form from nine fields to three
tickets.description: Six of the fields are never used after signup. The variant with three fields has already been tested.

visible.impactHint: A/B test last quarter: +11% completed signups.

hidden.explanation: Already validated by an experiment and nearly free to ship. The best value-per-point ticket in most backlogs.

tickets.title: Enforce MFA for admin accounts before the security audit
tickets.description: Audit fieldwork starts in three weeks and admin MFA is a failing control today. Four enterprise renewals require the finished report.

visible.impactHint: Audit fieldwork starts in 3 weeks.

hidden.explanation: A fixed audit date with renewals contractually tied to the result. Missing it is not an option.

tickets.title: Custom PDF report layout for Solstice Hotels
tickets.description: Solstice Hotels wants our reports in their corporate template, with their logo, fonts and a signature block. Their procurement team calls it a condition for renewal.

visible.impactHint: Solstice Hotels is our third largest account.

hidden.explanation: One customer's template, hard-coded into the product. Nobody else has asked. The 'condition' is a negotiating position: a paid services engagement or a plain export covers it.

tickets.title: Header briefly shows a stale account name after deploys
tickets.description: After the last two deploys, two users reported that the header showed another company's name for a moment. A refresh fixed it. Probably a caching quirk.

hidden.explanation: One customer seeing another customer's data is a cross-account leak, not a cosmetic glitch. If the cache mixes names it can mix anything.

tickets.title: Admins cannot free the seat of a deactivated user
tickets.description: When someone leaves a customer's company, their seat stays billed. Support removes these by hand on request.

hidden.explanation: Customers are paying for people who left, and they notice at renewal. A small fix removes a top ticket driver and a renewal objection.

tickets.title: Notify admins 30 days before annual renewal
tickets.description: Annual plans renew without warning. Admins who meant to change seats or plans find out from the card charge.

visible.impactHint: Surprise renewals drive 1 in 4 refund requests.

hidden.explanation: Prevents refunds and angry escalations with one scheduled email.

tickets.title: Usage dashboard for admins
tickets.description: Admins ask who on their team actually uses the product, so they can justify the spend internally.

hidden.explanation: Helps champions defend the renewal. Useful, but its effect is indirect.

tickets.title: In-app 'wall of love' with customer logos and quotes
tickets.description: Show logos and testimonials on the home screen so users see who else trusts us.

visible.impactHint: Social proof builds trust.

hidden.explanation: Social proof persuades buyers on the website. People inside the app already bought; it only takes space from their work.

tickets.title: Monthly usage report for account admins
tickets.description: Account managers build usage summaries by hand before each renewal. Admins would like to receive one automatically.

hidden.explanation: Helps renewals across the whole base and removes manual work. Moderate value.

tickets.title: Add indexes for the five slowest queries
tickets.description: Five queries account for most of the database load. All of them scan full tables.

visible.impactHint: p95 latency doubles at peak hours.

hidden.explanation: A small, well-understood change that every user feels at peak time.

tickets.title: Import from spreadsheets with column mapping
tickets.description: New customers arrive with their data in spreadsheets. The current import only accepts our own template, so onboarding calls are spent reformatting files.

visible.impactHint: Onboarding calls spend 40 minutes on manual import.

hidden.explanation: Every new account hits this wall on day one. High value, though it is a large piece of work.

tickets.title: Customers are billed for people who have left
tickets.description: In three renewal calls this month the admin opened with the same complaint: seats of former employees still on the invoice. They want to remove them themselves.

hidden.explanation: Same work as FLD-478 ("Admins cannot free the seat of a deactivated user"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Scheduled items fire at the wrong hour outside UTC
tickets.description: Anything scheduled is stored without a time zone. Users in other zones get reminders and reports hours early or late.

hidden.explanation: A correctness bug in a feature people rely on, affecting everyone outside one time zone. Cheap to fix.

tickets.title: Upgrade the web framework two major versions
tickets.description: The current version leaves security support in nine months. The upgrade touches every page and needs a full regression pass.

visible.impactHint: Security support ends in 9 months.

hidden.explanation: Necessary, not urgent: there are nine months of runway and it would eat most of a sprint. Plan it, do not squeeze it in.

tickets.title: Unsubscribe link shows a blank page in some email clients
tickets.description: A handful of recipients say the unsubscribe link does nothing in Outlook. They are still receiving our emails.

hidden.explanation: Ignoring unsubscribe requests breaks anti-spam law and gets sending domains blocklisted, which would also stop receipts and password resets.

tickets.title: White-label the product for Brightline Retail
tickets.description: Brightline Retail wants to resell us under their own name and domain, with our branding removed everywhere including emails.

visible.impactHint: Brightline Retail says they could bring 40 clients.

hidden.explanation: A new business model decided by one partner's promise. 'Could bring' is not a signed commitment, and the branding work touches every surface.

tickets.title: Mandatory 'cost centre code' field for Oakridge Partners
tickets.description: Oakridge Partners's finance team needs every record tagged with their internal cost centre code, validated against their list.

visible.impactHint: Oakridge Partners renews in two months.

hidden.explanation: A field only one account understands, added to forms everyone uses. Custom fields as a general feature would be a different, bigger ticket.

tickets.title: Activity log for account admins
tickets.description: Admins want to see who changed what and when. Security questionnaires from larger prospects ask for it explicitly.

visible.impactHint: Currently blocking two security reviews.

hidden.explanation: A genuine requirement for larger accounts, but it only matters to a slice of the pipeline and it is not small.

tickets.title: Read-only and custom roles
tickets.description: Every user is either an admin or a member. Larger teams need viewers, contractors and restricted roles before they can roll us out.

visible.impactHint: Named in 11 of the last 40 lost-deal notes.

hidden.explanation: A quarter of lost deals cite it. That is a pattern across the market, and it justifies a large ticket.

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Dark mode
tickets.description: The most upvoted item on the public feedback board. Users on social media ask for it every time we post.

visible.impactHint: 212 votes on the feedback board.

hidden.explanation: Votes measure the enthusiasm of a vocal few, not impact on activation or retention. Pleasant, never urgent.

tickets.title: Export includes items from projects the user was removed from
tickets.description: A customer noticed that a contractor's CSV export still contains two projects they no longer have access to. Minor inconsistency.

hidden.explanation: The export ignores permissions: anyone removed from a project can still download its data. That is an access-control hole, not an inconsistency.

midSprintEvents.title: Legal: the new consent rules apply from the 1st
midSprintEvents.description: Samir forwarded a note from the lawyers. The privacy authority's new guidance takes effect on the 1st, and the current consent screen does not meet it.

addedTicket.title: Update the consent screen to meet the new privacy guidance
addedTicket.description: Change the consent screen and stored consent records to match the new guidance before it takes effect on the 1st.

visible.impactHint: Takes effect on the 1st.

hidden.explanation: From the 1st the current screen is non-compliant for every user. A dated legal requirement goes in whatever it displaces.

hidden.guidance: Legal deadlines are constraints, not priorities to weigh. Take it in, then decide what leaves the sprint to pay for it.

midSprintEvents.title: Samir wants a demo feature for next week's investor meeting
midSprintEvents.description: Samir came back from a dinner with investors and wants a live map of customer activity on the home screen in time for next week's meeting. 'It only needs to look good.'

addedTicket.title: Live activity map for the investor demo
addedTicket.description: An animated world map on the home screen showing customer activity in real time, ready for next week's investor meeting.

visible.impactHint: It only needs to look good.

hidden.explanation: Built to impress in one meeting. It does nothing for customers and it would push out work that does.

hidden.guidance: Say no with a trade-off, not with a refusal: show exactly what would leave the sprint to make room, and offer a mock-up or a recorded demo instead. Seniority of the requester does not change the value of the ticket.
